items.b: ANTWERP'S ROUGH IMPORTS FELL TO 1,590,026 CARATS, THE LOWEST MONTH IN FIVE YEARS
items.t: July 2026 rough imports were $241,050,713 for 1.59 million carats, an average of $151.60 a carat against June's $88.63. The three thinnest months in AWDC's 55-month published series are May, June and July 2026, in that order. Against July 2025 the carats are down 49.01% and the value down 41.81%. The May to July average is $117.14 a carat.

items.b: PALLADIUM'S NINE-SESSION HOLD ENDED AT $1,381.00, AND THE DIVERGENCE WAS A SPREAD
items.t: Between 04:59 and 05:59 ET Kitco's bid moved $22.00, TradingEconomics $21.50 and CNBC $21.45. The 1.71% apparent gap is Kitco's bid measured against the others' mid, on a $40.00 bid-ask worth 2.896% of the bid. Written back at the bid, the convention this tape uses for the other three metals. Change on the held mark is +$45.00, or 3.3683%, across nine sessions.

items.b: $25.46 MILLION TO NEW ZEALAND, AND GOLD JEWELLERY CARRIED 93% OF THE RISE
items.t: GJEPC put India's FY2025-26 gem and jewellery exports to New Zealand at $25.46 million against $16.91 million, up 50.56%. Gold jewellery was $17.47 million, up 84%, which is about 93% of the whole increase on this desk's arithmetic. Lab-grown diamonds rose 2% to $0.63 million. The India-New Zealand agreement signed on 27 April is still not in force.

items.b: CHOW TAI FOOK'S COUNTER FELL A FOURTH SESSION TO 1,387 YUAN A GRAM
items.t: The board has given back 23 yuan since 25 August, or 1.6312%, carried identically today by cngoldprice.com and jinjia.com.cn. The brand's platinum jewellery counter is 711 yuan against 731 on 25 August, down 2.7360%, on a morning spot platinum rose 3.6894%. The boards are stamped 16:00 China time, four hours before this desk's press-time read.

items.b: INDIA'S 15% GOLD DUTY RAISED ₹10,463 CRORE IN 81 DAYS AND IMPORTS ROSE ANYWAY
items.t: The rate went from 6% to 15% on 13 May to protect dollar reserves. May imports rose nearly 34% and June-July imports were $6.13 billion against $5.81 billion, up 5.51%. April, ahead of the hike, was up nearly 82%. Reports on 26 August say a cut back to 6% is under review, on unnamed sources with no notification issued.

items.b: ₹5,000 NOW BUYS 0.294 GRAMS OF GOLD AT AN AHMEDABAD COUNTER
items.t: Gold is reported at ₹1.7 lakh per 10 grams against ₹1.02 lakh at last year's Raksha Bandhan, up 66.67%, and silver at ₹2.45 lakh a kilo against ₹1.17 lakh, up 109.40%. The source's claim that both metals more than doubled holds for silver and not for gold. Retailers are moving into 9-carat, which carries 40.9% of 22-carat's gold content.
